extension.summary: Fixes stale leftover system addon copies (e.g. xbmc.python) that silently block other addon installs
extension.description: On long-lived CoreELEC installs that have been through several major Kodi version upgrades, a handful of genuinely system/bundled addons (shipped in /usr/share/kodi/addons, which gets fully replaced on every OS update) can end up with an old leftover local copy in /storage/.kodi/addons (which deliberately survives every OS update untouched, by design, to protect user settings/addons) that Kodi keeps using instead of the current one shipped with the installed Kodi binary. This silently blocks installing any addon that requires a newer version of that dependency - most commonly xbmc.python itself - with no clear error shown anywhere. At every Kodi startup, this service compares each addon id that genuinely exists in /usr/share/kodi/addons against any local /storage/.kodi/addons copy of the same id; if the local one is older, it removes it so Kodi re-registers the current bundled version from /usr/share on the next restart. It only ever touches ids that are real bundled system addons (a short, stable list - about 45 on a typical CoreELEC box) and only when the local copy is strictly older, never a normal repo-installed addon and never a local copy that's equal or newer. A Kodi restart is needed after a fix is applied; a one-time notification says so, and the fix is confirmed (and the notification won't repeat) once the stale copy is actually gone after that restart.
extension.news: 1.2.0: also fixes any currently-incompatible addon whose own addon.xml <requires> declares an older xbmc.gui or xbmc.python version than what's actually installed - confirmed live on box oco 2026-10-20: after a CoreELEC major OS update (20.5 Nexus to 21.3 Omega) bumped the real xbmc.gui from 5.16.0 to 5.17.0, skin.aeon.nox.5 still declared "<import addon=\"xbmc.gui\" version=\"5.15.0\" />" and Kodi rejected it outright as "not compatible" despite 5.17.0 numerically satisfying that minimum - rewriting that one import line to match the real installed version exactly was the whole fix (box "oby" already had this exact one-line fix from an earlier, undocumented session; "oco" did not, which is how it was found). Clears the addon's cached incompatible DB row too, since a file edit alone was confirmed not enough on its own. 1.1.0: also self-heals stale local copies of this repo's own dependency modules (script.module.beautifulsoup4, script.module.soupsieve, etc.) by downloading the current version straight from this repo's zips and replacing the stale one directly - confirmed live on box oco that Kodi's normal "auto-upgrade a dependency during install" mechanism does not reliably fire for these, even after the xbmc.python fix on its own. Removed the xbmc.python <requires> import entirely (not just lowered it) - any version in the 2.x range turned out to make Kodi reject the whole addon as "not compatible" outright (a hard Python-2-era vs Python-3-era API mismatch, not just "too low"), and this addon's own code does not need a specific Python API floor anyway. 1.0.0: initial release. Root-caused on box "oco" (2026-10-19): xbmc.python was stuck at 2.26.0 in /storage/.kodi/addons since a 2019/2021-era install, despite the box running Kodi 20.5-Nexus (system copy 3.0.1) - this silently blocked installing script.cu.lrclyrics.fixed (requires xbmc.python >= 3.0.0) with no error anywhere in the GUI or log.
